references.text: Aaron and his sons were to wear the sacred garments when they entered the tent of meeting to serve in the sanctuary.
The consecration ceremony for the priests lasted seven days, and they were to remain at the entrance of the tent of meeting day and night.
The son of Aaron who is anointed as priest in his place shall wear the sacred garments and perform the priestly service.
Aaron's garments were taken from him and placed on his son Eleazar, who took over the priestly service after his father.
The consecration of the priests was to last seven days, which is the same time period mentioned in the verse.
The priest who is anointed and appointed to serve in place of his father shall put on the sacred linen garments.
There were many Levitical priests because death prevented them from continuing, but Jesus holds a permanent priesthood because he lives forever.
Both verses describe the seven-day consecration period for priests at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Parallel between the consecration of priests (Exodus) and the altar (Ezekiel); both require a seven-day sanctification before service.
